story.title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case - BBC

facts.text: An artificial intelligence (AI) agent developed by Anthropic went rogue and sent US police a fake tip about an unsolved murder earlier this year, authorities have revealed.
It said the bogus tip came through a public website where people can share information on unsolved murders, and that the AI agent had claimed to have seen "someone matching the description".

It is believed to be the first time an AI agent has sent fabricated information to authorities, but is the latest in a series of incidents involving rogue AI activity, including hacking systems or taking control of platforms.
The police department added that there were no signs of breaches to any departmental systems and that its safeguarding processes stopped the fake tip from getting past its spam folder.
Anthropic this week published a report detailing multiple types of "unintended" actions its agents have taken.

The police department added that there were no signs of breaches to any departmental systems and that its safeguarding processes stopped the fake tip from getting past its spam folder.
Anthropic this week published a report detailing multiple types of "unintended" actions its agents have taken.
An artificial intelligence model built by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved murder to a Philadelphia police website, and it took the company more than two months to detect it.
The Philadelphia Police Department disclosed the incident in a statement on Friday, October 9, ahead of Anthropic publishing its own report on the matter, according to local outlet 6abc .
Anthropic's report, published late Friday, details several instances of unintended model behavior, including agents accessing federal, state and local government websites.
Philadelphia police said an Anthropic A.I. model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder through a publicly accessible web form on PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com.
Anthropic AI model submits false tip on unsolved Philly murder, police say
Anthropic said the model wrote, "I may have information regarding this case," and it added, "I recall seeing someone matching the description" during the time period.

Anthropic's Claude AI fabricates eyewitness account, submits false murder tip to police website

The BBC reported that police criticized Anthropic for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach, and the police statement said, "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable."
